to.pē. 2433 9030
patippuri
oḷavi cu.turicāmip piḷḷi
tamatu ōyvaṟiyā uḻippāl  tamiḻ āyvuk kaḷattil uyarntu niṉṟavar. 20 ām nūṟṟāṇṭil tamiḻ maṟumalarccikku puttuyir ūṭṭiya tamiḻc cāṉṟōrkaḷuḷ muṉ variciyil niṟpavar. naṟṟiṇi, puṟanāṉūṟu, aiṅkuṟunūṟu, patiṟṟuppattu ākiya caṅka nūṟ celvaṅkaḷukku urivaḷam kaṇṭavar. civa peruṅkaṭalil mūḻkit tiḷittavar. urivēntar eṉṟu tamiḻulakam pōṟṟip pukaḻappaṭṭa oḷavi cu.turicāmip piḷḷi 1903il piṟantu 1981il maṟintār. 
 vāḻnta āṇṭukaḷ 78. eḻutiya nūlkaḷ 38. itaṉi  poruḷ vaḻip pirittu “urivēntar tamiḻttoki” eṉum talippil 28 tokutikaḷāka veḷi yiṭṭuḷḷōm.
illaṟa ēntalākavum, urinayam kaṇṭa uravōrākavum , naṟṟamiḻ nāvalarākavum, civa cittāntac cemmalākavum , niṟipukaḻ eytiya urivēntarāka vum, pulamiyilum perum pulamipeṟṟavarākavum tikaḻntu viḷaṅkiya ipperuntamiḻācāṉiṉ nūlkaḷ aṉittiyum oru cēra veḷiyiṭuvatil perumi koḷkiṟōm. ivaruṭiya nūlkaḷil  em kikkuk kiṭikkap peṟāta nūlkaḷ 5. maṟṟum ivar eḻutiya tiruvaruṭpā  nūlkaḷum it tokutikaḷil iṭam peṟavilli. 
  “ palvēṟu kālat tamiḻ ilakkiyaṅkaḷ, urikaḷ, varalāṟu, kalveṭṭu, camayaṅkaḷ eṉṟiṉṉa tuṟip palavaṟṟil niṟipulami peṟṟavar oḷavi cu .turicāmi avarkaḷ” eṉṟu mūtaṟiñar va.cupa. māṇikkam avarkaḷālum,
  “iravupakal tāṉaṟiyāṉ iṉtamiḻi vittu
	 varavu celavaṟiyāṉ vāḻvil - uramuṭiyāṉ
	 taṉkaṭaṉ tāynāṭṭu makkaṭ kuḻippatilē
	 muṉkaṭaṉ eṉṟurikkum ēṟu” 
eṉṟu pāvēntar pāratitācaṉ avarkaḷālum pōṟṟip pukaḻap paṭṭa ip peruntakiyiṉ nūlkaḷi aṇikalaṉkaḷākak kōrttu, muttumāliyākak  koṭuttuḷḷōm.   
 avar kālattil vāḻnta camakāla aṟiñarkaḷāl pōṟṟip pukaḻap paṭṭavar.  civa ulakil taṉakkeṉat taṉiyiṭattip peṟṟavar.  ivar eḻutiya aṉittu nūlkaḷ maṟṟum malarkaḷ, itaḻkaḷil veḷivanta kaṭṭurikaḷiyellām tēṭit tēṭi eṭuttu orē vīccil veḷiyiṭukiṟōm. 
ittokutikaḷ aṉittum mikacciṟappāka veḷivaruvataṟku muḻuottuḻippum utaviyum nalkiyavarkaḷ avaruṭiya tirumakaṉ oḷavi tu.naṭarācaṉ, marukar irā.kumaravēlaṉ, makaḷ vayiṟṟup peyartti tirumati vēṉilā sṭāliṉ ākiyōr āvar. ivarkaḷ it tamiḻttokikku takka matippuriyum aḷittu eṅkaḷukkup perumic cērttu uḷḷaṉar. ivarkaḷukku neñcam niṟinta naṉṟi
taṉ matippu iyakkattil pērīṭupāṭu koṇṭu  uḻitta ivvaruntamiḻaṟiñar tamiḻp pakivarit tam pakivarākak koṇṭa uyar maṉattiṉarāka vāḻntavar eṉpati niṉivil koṇṭu it toki  nūlkaḷi  ipperuntamiḻ aṟiñariṉ 
107  ām āṇṭu niṉivāka ulakat tamiḻarkaḷukkup payaṉpaṭum vakiyil  veḷiyiṭuvatil perumakiḻvu koḷkiṟōm. tamiḻ nūl patippil eṅkaḷiṉ inta ariya muyaṟcikkut tōḷ tantu utavuṅkaḷ.
naṉṟi
- patippāḷar

pēruri varinta peruntamiḻk kaṭal!
poṟputiyal - maṇikkuviyal
“	nūlukku nūlarumi kāṭṭuvatil nuṇṇaṟiñaṉ
mēlukkuc collavilli vērppalāt - tōlukkuḷ
uḷḷa cuḷikoṭukkum uṇmi uḻippāḷaṉ
aḷḷak kuṟiyāta āṟu”
eṉṟu pāvēntarum,
“payaṉuḷḷa varalāṟṟittanta tālē
	paraṇartāṉ, paraṇartāṉ tāṅkaḷ! vākku
nayaṅkāṭṭic cevikkuttēṉ tanta tālē
	nakkīrartāṉ tāṅkaḷ inta nāḷil
kayaṉmaṉṉar toḻutamoḻi kāttataṉāl - tol
	kāppiyartāṉ! kāppiyartāṉ tāṅkaḷ! eṅkum
tayaṅkāmal ceṉṟutamiḻ vaḷartta tālē
	tāṅkaḷav-oḷavitāṉ! oḷavi yētāṉ!”
eṉṟu pukaḻntatōṭu,
	“atiyaṉtāṉ iṉṟilli irunti runtāl
	aṭaṭāvō īteṉṉa vinti! iṅkē
  putiyatāyōr āṇoḷavi eṉavi yappāṉ”
eṉak kaṇṇīr malkak kallaṟi muṉ kaviyaracar mīrā urukiyatiyum nāṭu naṉkaṟiyum.
palvēṟu kālat tamiḻilakkiyaṅkaḷ, urikaḷ, varalāṟu, kalveṭṭu, camayaṅkaḷ eṉṟiṉṉa tuṟi palavaṟṟil niṟipulamiyum ceṟinta cintaṉi vaḷamum peṟṟavar urivēntar oḷavi turicāmi avarkaḷ. tūyacaṅkat tamiḻ naṭiyi eḻuttu
vaṉmiyilum colvaṉmiyilum oruṅku pēṇiya taṉit tamiḻppaṇpu oḷaviyiṉ aṟivāṇmikkuk kaṭṭiyaṅ kūṟum. eṭṭut tokiyuḷ aiṅkuṟunūṟu, naṟṟiṇi, puṟanāṉūṟu, patiṟṟuppattu eṉṟa nāṉku toki nūlkaṭkum uriviḷakkam ceytār. ivvuri viḷakkaṅkaḷil varalāṟṟuk kuṟippum kalveṭṭuk kuṟippum maṇṭik kiṭakkiṉṟaṉa. aiṅkuṟu nūṟṟuc ceyyuṭkaḷi innūṟṟāṇṭiṉ maraviyal vilaṅkiyal aṟivu taḻuvi nuṭpamāka viḷakkiya urittiṟaṉ pakkantōṟum paḷicciṭak kāṇalām. uri eḻutuvataṟku muṉ, ēṭukaḷ tēṭi mūlapāṭam tērntu terintu varampu ceytukōṭal ivartam uriyoḻuṅkākum. tamiḻ ilakkiya varalāṟṟil nāṉku caṅkat toki nūlkaṭku urikaṇṭavar eṉṟa taṉipperumiyar mūtaṟiñar oḷavi turicāmi āvār. itaṉāl urivēntar eṉṉum ciṟappup peyari maturi tiruvaḷḷuvar kaḻakam vaḻaṅkiṟṟu. paranta camayavaṟivum nuṇṇiya civa cittāntat teḷivum uṭiyavarātaliṉ civañāṉapōtattukkum ñāṉāmirtattukkum maṇimēkaliyiṉ camaya kātikaṭkum ariya urippaṇi ceytār. cittānta civatti uriyālum kaṭṭuriyālum kaṭṭaminta poḻivukaḷālum parappiya arumi nōkki ‘cittānta kalāniti’ eṉṟa camayappaṭṭatti aṟiñar vaḻaṅkiṉar. cilappatikāram, maṇimēkali, cīvakacintāmaṇi, cūḷāmaṇi, yacōtara kāviyam eṉṉum aintu kāppiyaṅkaḷiṉ ilakkiya muttukkaḷi oḷivīcac ceytavar. maturik kumaraṉār, cēramaṉṉar varalāṟu, varalāṟṟukkāṭcikaḷ, nantāviḷakku, oḷavit tamiḻ eṉṟiṉṉa urinaṭi nūlkaḷum tokuttaṟkuriya taṉikkaṭṭurikaḷum ivartam palpulamiyip paṟicāṟṟuvaṉa.
urivēntar uri variyum muṟi ōru taṉicciṟappu vāyntatu. poruḷ kūṟumpōtu āciriyar varalāṟṟiyum, avar pāṭutaṟku aminta cūḻniliyiyum, appāṭṭiṉ vāyilāka avar urikkak karutum uṭkōḷiyum ovvoru pāṭṭiṉ uriyilum muṉkūṭṭi eṭutturikkiṉṟār.
pāṇṭiyaṉ aṟivuṭinampiyiṉ pāṭṭukku uri kūṟuṅkāl, avaṉ varalāṟṟiyum, avaṉatu pāṭṭiṉ cūḻniliyiyum viriyak kūṟi, muṭivil, “ikkūṟṟu aṟakkaḻivuṭiyatāyiṉum poruṭpayaṉpaṭa varum ciṟappuṭittātalik kaṇṭa pāṇṭiyaṉ aṟivuṭi nampi, taṉ iyalpukku ottiyalvatu tērntu, ataṉi ippāṭṭiṭip peytu kūṟukiṉṟāṉ eṉṟu muṉmoḻintu, piṉpu pāṭṭit tarukiṉṟār. piṟitōriṭattē kapilar pāṭṭukkup poruḷāṉa nikaḻcciyi viḷakkik kāṭṭi, “neñcukkut tāṉ aṭimiyākātu taṉakku aḵtu aṭimiyāyt taṉ āṇikku aṭaṅki naṭakkumāṟu ceyyum talivaṉiṭattē viḷaṅkum perumiyum uraṉum kaṇṭa kapilar ippāṭṭiṉkaṇ uḷḷuṟuttup pāṭukiṉṟār” eṉṟu iyampukiṉṟār. ivvāṟu pāṭṭiṉ muṉṉuri amivatāl, paṭippōr uḷḷattil appāṭṭip paṭittu makiḻa vēṇṭum eṉṟa avā eḻuntu tūṇṭu kiṟatu.pāṭṭukkaḷam iṉitu paṭippataṟkēṟṟa uriya iṭattil coṟkaḷip pirittu ac ciṭṭiruppatu ikkālattu otta muṟiyākum. ataṉāl iraṇṭāyiram āṇṭukaṭku muṉ tōṉṟiya naṟṟiṇiyiṉ arumippāṭu ōraḷavu eḷimi eytukiṟatu.
karumpik kaṇukkaṇuvākat taṟittuc cuvikāṇpatu pōlap pāṭṭit toṭartoṭarākap pirittup poruḷ urippatu paḻiya urikārarkaḷāṉa parimēlaḻakar, nacciṉārkkiṉiyar mutaliyōr kikkoṇṭa muṟiyākum. ammuṟiyilēyē ivvurikaḷ amintiruppatāl, paṭikkumpōtu pala iṭaṅkaḷ, urivēntar uriyō parimēlaḻakar mutaliyōr uriyō eṉap paṉmuṟiyum nammi maruṭṭukiṉṟaṉa.
“ilakkaṇanūṟ perumparappum ilakkiyanūṟ
    peruṅkaṭalum ellām āyntu,
kalakkamaṟat tuṟipōkak kaṟṟuṇarnta
    perumpulamik kalvi yāḷar!
vilakkakalāt tarukkanūl, meypporuḷnūl,
     vaṭamoḻinūl, mēṟpāl nūlkaḷ
nalakkamikat teḷintuṇarntu nāṭuyya
      naṟṟamiḻ taḻikka vantār!”
eṉṟu pārāṭṭap peṟum perum pulamiyāḷarākiya arumpeṟal oḷaviyiṉ nūlaṭaṅkali aṅkiṅkellām tēṭiyalintu tiṭpamum nuṭpamum viḷaṅkap patitta pāṭu naṉiperitākum.
kalippolivum, karuttutteḷivum, potunōkkum polinta nam urivēntar, vaḷḷalāriṉ tiruvaruṭpā muḻumikkum pērurikaṇṭa peruñcelvam. iḵtu tamiḻp pēḻikkut tāṅkoṇā aruṭcelvamākum. nūluri, tiṟaṉuri, poḻivuri eṉṟa muvvarampālum tamiḻk kariyit tiṇṇitākkiya urivēntar oḷavi turicāmi avarkaḷiṉ pukaḻuriyi niṉintu avar nūlkaḷi nammutalvar kaliñar nāṭṭuṭimi ākkiyataṉ payaṉākat  ipputiyalit iṉiyamutu patippakam veḷiyiṭukiṉṟatu. iṉiyamutu patippaka urimiyāḷar, tamiḻmaṇ patippakattiṉ  urimiyāḷar kō.iḷavaḻakaṉāriṉ aruntavapputalvi i.tamiḻamutu āvār.   
īṭariya tamiḻārvap piḻampākavum, vīṟuṭiya tamiḻppatippu vēntarākavum viḷaṅkum naṇpar iḷavaḻakaṉ tām peṟṟa peruñcelvam muḻuvatiyum tamiḻiṉat taṇal taṇiyalākāteṉa naṟuneyyūṭṭi vaḷarppavar. tamiḻmaṇ patippakam avartam neñcak kaṉalukku vaḻikōluvatākum. avariṉ celvamakaḷār avar vaḻiyil naṭantu    iṉiyamutu patippakam vaḻi, mutal veḷiyīṭāka eṉtantiyāriṉ aṉittu ākkaṅkaḷiyum (tiruvaruṭpā tavira)  payaṉpeṟum vakiyil veḷiyiṭukiṟār. ippatippup putiyali - poṟkuviyali  tamiḻulakam iru kiyēnti varavēṟkum eṉṟē karutukiṟōm.
oḷavi naṭarācaṉ

nuḻivāyil
cemmoḻit tamiḻiṉ cevviyal ilakkiyap paṉuvalkaḷukku urivaḻaṅkiya cāṉṟōrkaḷuḷ talimakaṉāy niṟkum cemmal ‘urivēntar’ oḷavi cu.turicāmi piḷḷi avarkaḷāvār. pattuppāṭṭiṟkum, kalittokikkum cīvakacintāmaṇikkum  nalluri tanta nacciṉārkkiṉiyarukkup piṉ, āṟu nūṟṟāṇṭukaḷ kaḻittu, aiṅkuṟunūṟu, puṟanāṉūṟu, patiṟṟuppattu, naṟṟiṇi, yacōtara kāviyam ākiya nūlkaḷukku uriyeḻutiya perumi oḷavi avarkaḷiyē cārum.  caṅka nūlkaḷukkuc cemmiyāṉa uri tīṭṭiya mutal ‘tamiḻar’ ivar eṉṟu perumitam koḷḷalām.
eḻuttāṟṟalum pēccāṟṟalum mikka oḷavi 1903 ām āṇṭu cepṭampar aintām nāḷ tōṉṟi, 1981ām āṇṭu ēpral mūṉṟām nāḷ pukaḻuṭampu eytiyavar. tamiḻum civamum tam irukaṇkaḷākak koṇṭu iṟutivari ceyaṟpaṭṭavar.  cinti civaperumāṉic cintikka, cennā ainteḻuttu mantirattic ceppa, tirunīṟu neṟṟiyil tikaḻa, uruttirākkam mārpiṉil uruḷat taṉ muṉṉar irukkum ciṟu cāymēciyil tāḷkaḷik koṇṭu, uruṇṭu tiraṇṭa eḻutukōlit tiṟantu eḻutat toṭaṅkiṉārāṉāl maṇikkaṇakkil uṇṭi mutalāṉavi maṟantu kaṭṭurikaḷiyum, kaṉinta urikaḷiyum eḻutikkoṇṭē iruppār.  centamiḻ avar eḻutaṭṭum eṉṟu kāttiruppatupōl aruviyeṉak koṭṭum.  niṉivāṟṟalil vallavarātalāl eḻuntu ceṉṟu vēṟu nūlkaḷip pakkam puraṭṭi pārkka vēṇṭum eṉṉum nili avarukkiruntatilli.
ententa nūlkaḷukkuc cemmiyāṉa uriyilliyō avaṟṟiṟkē uriyeḻutuvatu eṉṉum koḷki uṭiyavar avar. ataṉāl atuvari cīriya uri kāṇappeṟāta aiṅkuṟunūṟu, patiṟṟuppattu ākiyavaṟṟiṟkum, muḻumiyāṉa uriyip peṟṟirāta puṟanāṉūṟṟukkum oḷavi uri varintār. piṉṉar naṟṟiṇikkup putturi tēvippaṭuvati aṟintu, muṉṉiya patippukaḷil irunta piḻikaḷi nīkkip putiya pāṭaṅkaḷit tērntu virivāṉa uriyiṉi eḻuti iru tokutikaḷāka veḷiyiṭṭār.
cittānta kalāniti eṉṉum perumi peṟṟa oḷavi, civañāṉapōtac ciṟṟuri viḷakkatti eḻutiyatōṭu, ‘irumpukkaṭali’ eṉak karutappeṟṟa ñāṉāmirta nūlukkum uri tīṭṭiṉār.  civa mānāṭukaḷukkut talimi tāṅkic coṟpoḻivukaḷ  nikaḻttiṉār.  tam urikaḷ palavaṟṟik kaṭṭurikaḷ ākkiṉār.  centamiḻc celvi, centamiḻ, kumarakuruparaṉ, cittāntam mutalāṉa pala itaḻkaḷukkuk kaṭṭurikaḷi vaḻaṅkiṉār.
peruntakip peṇṭir, maturik kumaraṉār, oḷavit tamiḻ, paraṇar mutalāṉa kaṭṭuri nūlkaḷi eḻutiṉār. avar ārāyccit tiṟaṉukkuc cāṉṟāka viḷaṅkum nūl ‘paṇṭi nāḷic cēramaṉṉar varalāṟu’ eṉṉum āyvu nūlākum.  aṇṇāmalip palkalik kaḻakattil oḷavi paṇiyāṟṟiyapōtu  ārāynteḻutiya ‘civa camaya ilakkiya varalāṟu’ attuṟiyil iṇiyaṟṟatāka iṉṟum viḷaṅkukiṟatu.
caṅka nūlkaḷukku oḷavi varinta uri kaṟṟōr aṉivaruṭiya neñciyum kavarntatākum.  ovvoru pāṭṭiyum alaci ārāyum paṇpuṭiyavar avar.  muṉṉiya uriyāciriyarkaḷ piḻipaṭṭiruppiṉ tayaṅkātu maṟuppuri taruvar.  takka pāṭa vēṟupāṭukaḷit tērnteṭuttu mūlattic cemmippaṭuttu vatil avarukku iṇiyāṉavar evarumilar.  ‘uḻutacāl vaḻiyē uḻum iḻuti neñciṉar’ allar.  perumpālum paḻamikku amiti kāṇpār.  atē nērattil putumikkum vaḻi ceyvār.
tamiḻōṭu āṅkilam, vaṭamoḻi, pāli mutalāṉavaṟṟik kaṟṟut tērntavar avar.  maṇimēkaliyiṉ iṟutip pakutikku uriyeḻutiya nili vantapōtu avar muṉintu pālimoḻiyik kaṟṟuṇarntu ataṉ piṉṉarē anta uriyiṉic ceytār eṉṟāl avaratu īṭupāṭṭuṇarvi naṉku uṇaralām.  eppōtum ētēṉum āṅkila nūlip paṭikkum iyalpuṭiyavar oḷavi avarkaḷ.  tirukkuṟaḷ paṟṟiya oḷaviyiṉ āṅkilac coṟpoḻivu nūlāka accil vantapōtu palarāl pārāṭṭap peṟṟami avartam āṅkilap pulamikkuc cāṉṟu pakarvatākum.  camaya nūlkaḷukku uriyeḻutuṅkāl vaṭamoḻi nūlkaḷiliruntu mēṟkōḷ kāṭṭuvatum, karuttukaḷi viḷakkuvatum avar iyalpu.  atumaṭṭumaṉṟi, oḷavi avarkaḷ caṭṭanūl nuṇukkaṅkaḷiyum kaṟṟaṟinta pulamic celvar.
oḷavi avarkaḷ kaṭṭuri puṉiyum vaṉmi peṟṟavar.  kalipayil teḷivu avarpāluṇṭu.  nuṇmāṇ nuḻipulattōṭu avar tīṭṭiya kaṭṭurikaḷ eṇṇila. avi caṅka ilakkiyap poruḷ paṟṟiyaṉa āyiṉum, camayac cāṉṟōr paṟṟiyaṉa āyiṉum putiya ceytikaḷ avaṟṟil alipōl puraṇṭu varum.  oḷavi naṭi taṉinaṭi.  aṟivu nuṭpattiyum karuttāḻattiyum antac cemmānta naṭiyil avar koṇṭuvantu tarumpōtu kaṟpār uḷḷam evvāṟu iruppārō, atippōṉṟē avar tamiḻ naṭiyum cintaṉip pōkkum amintiruntatu viyappukkuriya oṉṟu.
oḷavi āṟṟiya aruntamiḻp paṇikaḷuḷ taliyāyatu paḻantamiḻ nūlkaḷukku aṟivārnta urikaḷi vakuttut tantamiyē ākum.  etaṉiyum kāytal uvattaliṉṟi cīrtūkkip pārkkum naṭunilip pōkku avariṭam ūṉṟiyirunta oru paṇpu.  avar uri ciṟantamintataṟkāṉa kāraṇam iraṇṭu.  mutalāvatu, viṇava urikaḷil kāṇappeṟṟa ‘patacāram’ kūṟum muṟi.  tām uriyeḻutiya aṉittup paṉuvalkaḷilum kāṇappeṟṟa coṟṟoṭarkaḷi intap patacāra muṟiyilē aṇuki ariya ceytikaḷi aḷittuḷḷār.  iraṇṭāvatu, caṭṭa nuṇukkaṅkaḷit terivikkum nūlkaḷilaminta āyvurikaḷum tīrppurikaḷum avartam tamiḻ āyvukkut tuṇi niṉṟa tiṟam.  ‘jūrispurūṭaṉs’ ‘lā āḵp ṭārṭs’ mutalāṉavi paṟṟiya āṅkila nūlkaḷit tām paṭittatōṭu eṉṉip pōṉṟavarkaḷiyum paṭikka vittār.  vaṭamoḻit tarukkamum vēṟupiṟa aḷavi nūlkaḷum palvakic camaya aṟivum avar uriyiṉ cemmikkut tuṇi niṉṟaṉa.  aṉittiṟkum mēlāka varalāṟṟuṇarvu illāta ilakkiya aṟivu payaṉaṟṟatu, ilakkiyap payiṟci illāta varalāṟṟāyvu vīṇāṉatu eṉṉum karuttuṭiyavar avar.  ātalāl eṇṇaṟṟa varalāṟṟu nūlkaḷiyum, āyirakkaṇakkāṉa kalveṭṭukaḷiyum āḻntu paṭittu, maṉattiliruttit tām ilakkiyattiṟku uri varintapōtu naṉku payaṉpaṭuttik koṇṭār.  ñāṉacampantap peruntakiyiṉ tiruvōttūrt tēvārat tiruppatikattiṟku mutaṉmutalāka uriyeḻutat toṭaṅkiya kālantoṭṭu iṟutiyāka vaṭalūr vaḷḷaliṉ tiruvaruṭpāviṟkup pēruri eḻuti muṭikkum variyilum, varalāṟu, kalveṭṭu, tarukkam, ilakkaṇam mutalāṉavaṟṟiṉ aṭippaṭiyilēyē urikaḷi eḻutiṉār.  tēvippaṭumpoḻutu uyiriyal, payiriyal, uḷaviyal tuṟi nūlkaḷiliruntum viḷakkaṅkaḷi aḷikkat tavaṟavilli.  ivaṟṟi avartam aiṅkuṟunūṟṟu virivuri teḷivupaṭuttum.
oḷavi avarkaḷiṉ nuṭpa urikku oru cāṉṟu kāṭṭalām.  avaruṭiya naṟṟiṇip patippu veḷivarumvari atil kaṭavuḷ vāḻttup pāṭalāka aminta ‘mānilañ cēvaṭi yāka’ eṉṉum pāṭalit tirumāṟku uriyatākavē aṉivarum karutiṉar.  piṉṉattūrār tam uriyil avvāṟē eḻuti iruntār.  intap pāṭali iyaṟṟiyavar pāratam pāṭiya peruntēvaṉār.  ivarē vēṟu cila caṅkattoki nūlkaḷukkum kaṭavuḷ vāḻttu iyaṟṟiyavar.  avaṟṟilellām civaṉip pāṭiyavar naṟṟiṇiyil maṭṭum vēṟu iṟivaṉip pāṭuvarō eṉṟu cintitta oḷavi, muḻuppāṭalukkum civaneṟiyilēyē uriyi eḻutiṉār.
oḷavi uri amikkum pāṅkē taṉittaṉmiyāṉatu.  mutalil pāṭalip pāṭiya āciriyar peyar paṟṟiyum avartam ūrpaṟṟiyum viḷakkam taruvar.  tēvippaṭṭāl kalveṭṭu mutalāṉavaṟṟiṉ tuṇikoṇṭu peyarkaḷic cemmip paṭuttuvar.  tumpi cokiṉaṉār ivar āyvāl ‘tumpic cokiṉaṉār’ āṉār.  neṭuṅkaḻuttup paraṇar oḷaviyāl ‘neṭuṅkaḷattup paraṇar’  eṉṟāṉār.  paḻiya māṟpittiyār oḷavi uriyil ‘mārip pittiyār’ āka māṟiṉār.  veṟipāṭiya kāmakkaṇṇiyār oḷaviyiṉ karampaṭṭut tūymiyāki ‘veṟipāṭiya kāmakkāṇiyār’ āṉār.  ivvāṟu ettaṉiyō caṅkap peyarkaḷ ivarāl cemmi aṭintuḷḷaṉa.
aṭutta niliyil, pāṭaṟ piṉṉaṇic cūḻali nayampaṭa uriyāṭaṟ pōkkil eḻutuvar.  ataṉ piṉ pāṭal  muḻutum cīrpirittut tarappaṭum. aṭuttu, pāṭal toṭarkaḷukkup patavurip pōkkil viḷakkam amiyum.  piṉṉar ētukkaḷālum eṭuttukkāṭṭukaḷālum coṟṟoṭarp poruḷkaḷi viḷakki eḻutuvar.  tēvippaṭum iṭaṅkaḷil takka ilakkaṇak kuṟippu kaḷiyum mēṟkōḷkaḷiyum tavaṟātu vaḻaṅkuvar.  uḷḷuṟip poruḷ ētēṉum pāṭalil irukkumāṉāl avaṟṟit teḷivu paṭuttuvar. muṉpiṉ varum pāṭal toṭarkaḷi naṉkāyntu ‘viṉimuṭipu’ taruvatu avar vaḻakkam.  iṟutiyākap pāṭaliṉkaṇ aminta meyppāṭu īteṉṟum, payaṉ īteṉṟum teḷivu paṭuttuvar.
oḷaviyiṉ urinuṭpattiṟku oru cāṉṟu.  ‘pakivar pul ārka’ eṉpatu aiṅkuṟunūṟṟu nāṉkām pāṭalil varum oru toṭar.  maṉitar pul ārtal uṇṭō eṉṉum viṉā eḻukiṟatu.  eṉavē, uriyil ‘pakivar tam perumitam iḻantu pullaricic cōṟuṇka’ eṉa viḷakkam taruvar.  ikkaruttē koṇṭu, cēṉāvariyarum ‘puṟṟiṉṟal uyartiṇikku iyipiṉṟu eṉappaṭātu’ eṉṟār eṉa mēṟkōḷ kāṭṭuvar.  maṟṟoru pāṭṭil ‘mutalip pōttu muḻumīṉ ārum’ eṉa varukiṟatu. itil muḻumīṉ eṉpataṟku ‘muḻu mīṉiyum’ eṉṟu poruḷ eḻutātu, ‘iṉi vaḷarcci yilliyāmāṟu muṟṟa mutirnta mīṉ” eṉṟu uriyeḻutiya tiṟam aṟiyattakkatu.
oḷavi iḷampūraṇar, nacciṉārkkiṉiyar mutalāṉa paḻiya uriyāciriyarkaḷiyum maṟukkum āṟṟal uṭiyavar.  cāṉṟāka, ‘maṉinaṭu vayali’ (aiṅ.11) eṉṉum pāṭali iḷampūraṇar ‘kiḻavaṉi makaṭūup pulampu peritākaliṉ, alamaruḷ perukiya kāmattu mikutiyum’ eṉpataṟku eṭuttukkāṭṭuvar.  āṉāl, oḷavi ati maṟuttu, “maṟṟu, ippāṭṭu, alamaruḷ  perukiya kāmattu mikutikkaṇ nikaḻum kūṟṟākātu talimakaṉ koṭumikku amiti yuṇarntu orumaruṅku amitalum, avaṉ pirivāṟṟāmiyit tōḷmēl ēṟṟi amiyāmikku ētu kāṭṭutalum cuṭṭi niṟṟaliṉ, avar kūṟuvatu poruntāmi yaṟika” eṉṟu iṉimiyāka eṭutturippar.
“taṉ pārpput tiṉṉum aṉpil mutali” eṉṉum pāṭal talivaṉiyum vāyilkaḷiyum ikaḻntu talivi kūṟuvatākum.  āṉāl, itaṉip pērāciriyarum, nacciṉārkkiṉiyarum tattam tolkāppiya urikaḷil tōḻi kūṟṟu eṉṟu terivittuḷḷaṉar.  oḷavi ivaṟṟi nayampaṭa maṟuttu viḷakkam kūṟit ‘tōḻi kūṟṟeṉṟal nirampāmi aṟika’ eṉṟu teḷivuṟuttuvar.  ivvāṟu iḷampūraṇar, pērāciriyar, nacciṉārkkiṉiyar uḷḷiṭṭa aṉivariyum takka cāṉṟukaḷōṭu maṟutturikkum tiṟam karutiyum uriviḷakkac cemmi karutiyum ikkālac cāṉṟōr aṉivarum oḷaviyi ‘urivēntar’ eṉap pōṟṟiṉar.
oḷavi ovvoru nūlukkum eḻutiya urikaḷiṉ māṇpukaḷi eṭutturippiṉ perunūlāka viriyum.  tokuttuk kūṟa virumpiṉālō eñci niṟkum.  kaṟpōr tāmē virumpi nukarntu tuyppiṉ urit tiṟaṉkaḷik kaṇṭuṇarntu viyantu niṟpar eṉpatu tiṇṇam.
oḷaviyiṉ aṉittu urinūlkaḷiyum, kaṭṭuri nūlkaḷiyum, ilakkiya varalāṟṟu nūlkaḷiyum, pērurikaḷiyum, kaviṉmiku taṉik kaṭṭurikaḷiyum, piṟavaṟṟiyum pakuttum tokuttum koṇṭuvarutal eṉpatu mērumaliyik kikkuḷ aṭakkum perumpaṇi.  tamiḻīḻam toṭaṅki ayalnāṭukaḷ palavaṟṟilum, tamiḻnāṭṭiṉ mūli muṭukkukaḷilum āka, eṅkeṅkō citaṟikkiṭanta ariya kaṭṭurikaḷiyellām tēṭittiraṭṭit takka vakiyil patippikkum paṇiyil iṉiyamutu patippakam muyaṉṟu veṟṟi peṟṟuḷḷatu.  oḷavi nūlkaḷit tokuppatōṭu nillāmal muṟṟilum paṭittuṇarntu tuyttu makiḻntu tokuti tokutikaḷākap pakuttu veḷiyiṭum iṉiyamutu patippakam nam aṉivaruṭiya matippiṟkum pārāṭṭiṟkum naṉṟikkum uriyatu.  ippatippakattiṉ urimiyāḷar celvi i.tamiḻamutu tamiḻmaṇ patippakattiṉ urimiyāḷariṉ makaḷ āvār. vāḻka avartam tamiḻppaṇi.  vaḷarka avartam tamiḻttoṇṭu.  ulakeṅkum malarka tamiḻāṭci. vaḷampeṟuka. ittokuppukaḷ urivēntar tamiḻttoki eṉum talippil ‘iṉiyamutu’ patippakattiṉ vaḻiyāka veḷivaruvati varavēṟṟu tamiḻulakam tāṅkip piṭikkaṭṭum. tūkki niṟuttaṭṭum eṉṟu neñcāra vāḻttukiṟēṉ.
 muṉivar irā.kumaravēlaṉ

taṇṭamiḻācāṉ urivēntar
urivēntar oḷavi. turicāmi avarkaḷ, poṉṟāp pukaḻuṭiya pintamiḻc cāṉṟōr āvār. ‘urivēntar’ eṉavum, civa cittānta kalāniti eṉavum centamiḻp pulam ivaric cemmāntu aḻikkiṟatu. naṉṉeṟip paṭarum toṉṉalap poruḷviḷakkam kāṭṭi nūlukku nūlarumi ceytu eññāṉṟum nilitta pukaḻ īṭṭiya urivēntariṉ naṟṟiṟam vāynta coṟṟamiḻ nūlkaḷi vaki tokippaṭutti veḷiyiṭum tamiḻmaṇ patippakattāriṉ aruntoṇṭu aḷappariyatākum.
oḷavikkīnta arunellik kaṉiyi aritiṉ muyaṉṟu peṟṟavaṉ atiyamāṉ. atupōl iṉiyamutu patippakam oḷavi turicāmi avarkaḷiṉ kaṉiyamutu kaṭṭurikaḷiyum, ilakkiya nūlurikaḷiyum, tiṟaṉāyvu urikaḷiyum peritum muyaṉṟu kaṇṭaṟintu tokuttu veḷiyiṭṭuḷḷaṉar. ivartam arumperumpaṇi, tamiḻulakam talimēṟ koḷaṟkuriyatākum.
naṉipulamicāl cāṉṟōr uṭiyatu toṇṭi nāṭu; appakutiyil aminta tiṇṭivaṉattiṟku arukil uḷḷa oḷaviyārkuppattil 1903-ām āṇṭu teḷḷu tamiḻnaṭikku oru tuḷḷal piṟantatu.  aruḷtiru cuntarampiḷḷi, cantiramati ammiyār ākiya iṇiyarukku aintām makaṉāka (iraṭṭik kuḻanti - uṭaṉ piṟantatu peṇmakavu)p piṟantār. ñāṉap pāluṇṭa campantap perumāṉpōṉṟu iḷamiyilēyē oḷavi avarkaḷ  āṟṟal niṟintu viḷaṅkiṉār. tiṇṭivaṉattil tamatu paḷḷippaṭippi muṭittu vēlūril palkalip paṭippit toṭarntār. āyiṉ iṭinilip palkali paṭikkum niliyil paṭippit toṭara iyalāmaṟ pōyiṟṟu.
eṉavē, urivēntar tūymip paṇiyāḷarākap paṇiyēṟṟār; cila mātaṅkaḷē appoṟuppil iruntavar mīṇṭum tam kalviyit toṭarntār. tamiḻ mītūrnta aḷapparum paṟṟāl karantit tamiḻc caṅkat talivar tamiḻavēḷ umā makēcuvaram piḷḷi, na.mu.vēṅkaṭacāmi nāṭṭār mutalāṉa tamiḻp pērācāṉkaḷiṭam payiṉṟār; vittuvāṉ paṭṭamum peṟṟār. urivēntar, centamiḻk kalviyip pōṉṟē āṅkilap pulamiyum peṟṟiruntār.
“	kulaṉaruḷ teyvam koḷkimēṉmi
kalipayil teḷivu kaṭṭuri vaṉmi
nilamali niṟikōl malarnikar māṭciyum
amipavaṉ nūluri āciriyaṉ”
eṉum  ilakkaṇam muḻumiyum amiyap peṟṟavar urivēntar.
uyarnilip paḷḷikaḷ, tiruppati tiruvēṅkaṭavaṉ kīḻtticik kallūri, citamparam aṇṇāmali palkalik kaḻakam, maturi tiyākarāyar kallūri eṉa ivartam āciriyap paṇikkālam amintatu. āciriyar paṇiyil, taṉ āṟṟalit tiṟampaṭa veḷippaṭuttiṉār. eṉavē, pulavar. kā. kōvintaṉ, vittuvāṉ mā.irākavaṉ mutalāṉa talimāṇākkarkaḷi uruvākkiṉār. itaṉōṭamiyātu, eḻuttup paṇiyilum mikunta ārvattōṭum , tamiḻāḻattōṭum urivēntar īṭupaṭṭār. avar caṅka ilakkiya urikaḷ, kāppiyac curukkaṅkaḷ, varalāṟṟu nūlkaḷ, civacittānta nūlkaḷ eṉap paltiṟappaṭṭa nūlkaḷ eḻutiṉār.
tam eḻuttup paṇiyāl, tamiḻ kūṟu nallulakam pōṟṟip pārāṭṭum perumi peṟṟār urivēntar. oḷaviyavarkaḷ  tam nūlkaḷ vāyilāka putumic cintaṉikaḷi ulakiṟku neṟikāṭṭi uyvittār. poṉṉēpōl pōṟṟaṟkuriya muṉṉōr moḻip poruḷil potintuḷḷa māṉiṭaviyal, aṟiviyal, poruḷiyal, vilaṅkiyal, varalāṟu, araciyal eṉap paṉṉaruñ ceytikaḷi uri kūṟumukattāṉ eḷiyōrum uṇarumpaṭic ceytavar urivēntar.
eṭuttukkāṭṭāka, camaṇacamayac cāṉṟōrkaḷ coṟ pōril vallavarkaḷ eṉṟum kūṟumiṭattu urivēntar pala cāṉṟukaḷ kāṭṭi valiyuṟuttukiṟār.
“iṉi, camaṇa camayac cāṉṟōrkaḷip pārāṭṭum kalveṭṭukkaḷ palavum, avartam coṟpōr vaṉmiyiṉiyē peritum eṭuttōtukiṉṟaṉa. ciravaṇapelakōlāvil kāṇappaṭum kalveṭṭukaḷ ellāvaṟṟilum ivarkaḷ piṟa camayattavarōṭu coṟpōr ceytu peṟṟa veṟṟic ciṟappiyē vitantōtuvatik kāṇkiṉṟōm. piṟa camayattavar palarum civarum, pācupatarum, puttarum, kāpālikarumākavē kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉar. irāṭṭirakūṭa aracaruḷ oruvaṉeṉṟu karutappaṭum kiruṣṇarāyareṉṉum aracaṉ intirananti eṉṉum cāṉṟōri nōkki umatu peyar yātu? eṉṟu kēṭka, avar taṉ peyar paravātimallaṉ eṉpatu eṉṟu kūṟiyiruppatu oru nalla cāṉṟākum. tiruñāṉa campantarum avarkaḷic ‘cāvāyum vātucey cāvār” (147:9) eṉpatu kāṇka. ivaṟṟāl camaṇac cāṉṟōr coṟpōril pērārvamuṭiyavar eṉpatu peṟappaṭum. paṭavē, tōlā moḻit tēvarum camaṇ cāṉṟōrātalāl coṟpōril mikka ārvam koṇṭiruppār eṉṟeṇṇutaṟku iṭamum, tōlāmoḻit tēvar eṉṉum peyarāl avveṇṇattiṟkup paṟṟukkōṭum peṟukiṉṟōm. innūṟkaṇ, ‘tōlā nāviṉ cuccutaṉ’ (41) ‘kaṟṟavaṉ kaṟṟavaṉ karutum kaṭṭurikku uṟṟaṉa uṟṟa uytturikkum āṟṟalāṉ (150) eṉpaṉa mutalāka varuvaṉa akkaruttukku ātaravu tarukiṉṟaṉa. nakiccuvi paṟṟiyuri nikaḻntapōtum ivvāciriyar coṟpōrē poruḷākak koṇṭu,
“	vātam vellum vakiyātatu veṉṉil
ōti vella luṟuvārkaḷi eṉki
kōtukoṇṭa vaṭiviṉ taṭiyālē
mōti velvaṉ uri muṟṟuṟa eṉṟāṉ’
eṉpatum piṟavum ivarkkuc coṟpōrk kaṇ irunta vēṭki ittaṉmit teṉpati vaṟpuṟuttukiṉṟaṉa.

nīriṉum āraḷaviṉatāyp pulamiyum, maliyiṉum māṉap peritāy naṟpaṇpum vāykkap peṟṟavar urivēntar. ivartam naṉṟi maṟavāp paṇpiṟku ōr eṭuttuk kāṭṭāka oru ceytiyik kūṟalām. karantit tamiḻc caṅkattil taṉṉip pōṟṟip puranta tamiḻavēḷ umā makēcuvaram piḷḷiyiṉ niṉivu nāḷil uṇṇānōṉpum, muṉa nōṉpum iruttali vaḻakkamākak koṇṭiruntār.

   avvap pō tayarnta kāli

    iṉiyāri yuṟuvēm; antō

    uḷam tēyntu citikiṉṟēmāl”

INTRODUCTION
Tiru Avvi Duriswamy Pilli of the Annamali University is well known as the modern commentator on Sangam works. He now gives the world of Tamil Scholars his commentary on Patirruppattu.
Patirruppattu is the only avilable source book of ancient Cera history. Among all the Sangam works this is unique in being a Collection of the poems on Ceras. Ten great poets had sung the greatness of ten great Cera kings. Unfortunately of the hundred verses, the first ten and the last ten, probably singing the glories of Utiyan and Yanikkan Mantaram Ceral Irumpori respectively, are missing. There were two ruling Cera families that of Utian and that of Antuvan, the former being the senior and the min Cera line of Vanchi; the latter being the Irumpori line of Tondi. The second Ten and the third Tens belong to the two sons of Uthiyan viz., Imaya Varamban Netun Ceral Athan and Palyanic - Celkezhu Kuttuvan. The fourth, the fifith and the sixth Tens relate respectively to the sons of Netun Ceral Athan viz., Kalamkay-k-kanni Nar Muti-c-ceral, Katal Pirakkottiya Cenkuttuvan and Atukot-Pattu-c-ceral Athan. The rest of the book relate to the Irumpori family; the VII Ten belongs to Selvakkatunko Vazhi Athan, the VIII Ten to Perum Ceral Irumpori, the conqueror of Thakatur and the IV Ten to Ilam Ceral Irumpori, the son, the grandson and the great grandson respecvitvely of Antuvan Ceral.
Various places of importance, the great chiefs and chieftins, the foreigners like Yavanas, the warfare and important battlefields, the fivefold classification of the country and other geographical detils are all alluded to in this anthology. The poets of this anthology and the literary patronage of the Ceras are not myths. Paranan Kannam Kannan Katu, Vezhakkadu (Umbarkadu) and Kakkiyur, still existing in Malayalam country, bear testimony to the conferment of Jaghirs on the Poets Paranar, Kumattur Kannanar and Kakki-p-Padiniyar by the Cera kings, Cenkuttuvan, Imayavaramban Netun Ceral Athan, and Atukotpattu-c-Ceral Athan respectively.
This book is important as revealing the culture, the custom and practice, the political and military life of the Tamil land; of the first few centuries of the Christian era. It is interesting to note that the conception of the fundamental unity of India, from Himalayas to Cape Comorin, goes back, to the poems of the sangam Age ( verse 1 and 43 of this anthology). Politics had become, by that time, an all India Science and the Yagas, varying according to the gradation of sovereignty, were believed to have a magical influence in establishing an ever expanding empire.  This inspired the ambitious kings of Tamil land to perform the Royal sacrifices; and the study of their sacred texts and related literature became very popular. Further, the political unrest in the North drove the Sanskrit, Pali and Prakrit scholars to South India. Manimekali, the Tamil epic reveals the Taml land as a centre of all-India learning, with its intellectual capital at Kanchipuram. The beginning of this development is seen in Patirruppattu itself.
The Yagas are mentioned in many places. The Rajasuya was not unknown; there was a Cola of the name Rajasuyam Vetta Peru Nar Killi i.e. Nal Killi the Great who had performed the Rajasuya Yaga. There was the great Pandya of many yagas viz. Palyakacali Muthu Kutumi-p-Peru Vazhuthi. The Ceras, as seen from this book, were no exceptions. The Putra Kameshti yaga is, it may be suggested, mentioned in poem No.74 by Arisilkizhar, a Non-Brahmin poet. There we learn that the queen donned on her beautiful shoulders a circular skin of the stag, well cut out and decked with pearls and precious stones.Was the skin made thus into a valuable amulet? In the Atharva Veda are two charms for obtining a son ( III 23 & VI.11). The second of these mantras is relevant to the study of this Putra-kameshti. This consists of three parts and when the third part, which runs thus “May Prajapati elsewhere afford the birth of a female but here shall bestow a man” was recited, according to the sutras (Kans 35-9) which explin the procedure, “The fire is surrounded with the wool of a male animal and the wool is tied upon the woman” (probably as an amulet). Instead of the wool we find the skin of the stag, the male animal, being used in the sacrifice performed by the Cera king.
This reference to this Putra-kameshti is very important. The question is very often rised whether the Cera who ruled over a country where the MarumakkalTayam or matriarchal succession now reigns supreme, were following the law of Makkal Tayam or patriarchal succession, as their colleagues the Colas and the Pandyas did or were following the law of Marumakkal Tayam, as followed of the kings of Malayalam today. The wife of the king under the Marumakkal Tayam is never called the Queen. InPattirruppattu, every cera king is prised as the husband of the chaste consort. But his does not help us to decide the issue rised. The Putra-kameshti poem, however, conclusively proves, it was the son of the consort that becomes the king, thus establishing beyond doubt the patriarchal succession of these kings. There is one other difficulty, for the Padikam speaks of the mothers of these kings as “ Velavikoman Pathuman Devi” etc.  It is this kind of expression that has really created the confusion. Devi ordinarily means a wife, this phrase will then denote a wife of  a Velir chief Pathuman etc. How can the wife of a chief be also wife of the Cera King? This leads some scholars to assume that the succession was matriarchal where the mother of the ruling prince is never the wife of a king. But as this theory runs counter to the explicit statement of the Putra kameshti poem. One has to explin the word according to Thiru T.V.Sadasiva Pandarathar as meaning “dughter,” a usage made clear by such phrases as Cera ma Devi, Pancavan ma Devi, all wives of Colas and not of Ceras or Pandyas. Or Ceran ma devi etc. may be an elliptical shorthand expression for “The great Cola queen, the dughter of the Pandya or Cera.” Names like Sentan korran or Kiran Korran etc. mean Korran son of Centan or Kiran. Therefore Patuman Ma Devi mean the Queen, the dughter of Pathuman. One is justified in referring to the usage of the Imperial Cola Inscriptions in view of the close kinship that exists between the Meykkirtis of the later Colas and the Patikams of Patirruppattu as explined by Tiru T.V.Sadasiva Pandarathar in his short introduction to the present commentary.
In other places also, the Cera kings are prised in Patirruppattu for bringing forth children. The theory of three debts or duties to the Devas, the ancestors, and the learned, to be discharged respectively, by every man, by performing sacrifices, by bringing forth children, and by learning the ancient texts, it, as seen by this very poem and poem No. 70 as old as the Sangam age. Therefore, when Parimelazhagar speaks of this in his commentary on the chapter on Children in Tirukkutal, he is not going aginst any Tamil tradition.
There is an old commentary on Patirruppattu, whose importance cannot be easily exaggerated; but to the modern reader it is but a series of algebracial formula. The present commentary explins all that is necessary for elucidating the text for the man in the street - the defied abstraction of modern democracy; and serves, therefore, at a valuable key for unlocking the closely preserved treasure - chest of the old commentary.
The Sangam poets cught the spirit of the poetic moment and enshrined it in the most appropriate and correct poetic phrase, afrid of spoiling its effect by any elaboration. Brevity is the life of their poetry. This explins why the anthologies of the Sangam verses are arranged according to the length of verses as Kurum Togi, Nedun Togi, Aim Kuru Nuru etc. In every poem there is heart or life centre - a beautiful phrase which is the very quint - essence of the poem and this phrase by common acceptance and appreciation, becomes according to Sangam usage the very name of the verse. This is seen in every one of the verses in the present work. The new commentary has brought out the poetic significance of all these poetic phrases, thus helping us to understand the poetic theory of the Sangam age.
On an occasion like this, one cannot but think with reverential gratitude, of the late lamented Dr. Swaminatha Aiyar, but for whose untiring zeal and toil we could not be boasting either of Patirruppattu or its ancient commentary. What has been thus made avilable is now made more and more popular by the present commentator.  My friend Tiru Vellivaranan has brought out the importance of the new commentary. Whether one agrees with all the points or not one has to agree that this commentary is very valuable for a close study of the ancient work by the modern man. I deem it, therefore, a great privilege, as desired by my friend Thiru Avvi Duriswami Pilli, to introduce, with heartfelt thanks, this work, to the ever grateful public of Tamil land.
Madras

muṉṉuri
	kaṟṟataṉā lāya payaṉeṉkol vālaṟivaṉ 
	naṟṟāḷ toḻāar eṉiṉ.
caṅkat tokinūlkaḷ eṭṭuttokiyum pattup pāṭṭumeṉa vakiyāl  iraṇṭākiyum, viriyāl patiṉeṭṭā kiyum nilavuvaṉavākum. ivaṟṟuḷ patiṟṟuppatteṉpatu eṭṭuttokiyuḷ oṉṟākum. itu pappattāka aminta pattukkaḷ pattuk koṇṭateṉṟum, nūṟu pāṭṭukkaḷ koṇṭateṉṟum patiṟṟuppattu eṉappaṭum peyarālē aṟiyalām. itaṉ ovvoru pattum ovvoru cēra vēn taṉip paṟṟi vēṟu vēṟu āciriyaṉmārāl pāṭappaṭṭuḷatu. inta āciriyaṉmārkaḷum cēravēntarkaḷum oru kālattavarākavum vēṟu vēṟu kālattavarākavum karutappaṭu kiṉṟaṉar. patiṟṟuppat teṉṉum peyar ippāṭṭukkaḷip pappattāka eṭuttut tokuttōrāl iṭappeṟṟa peyarātal vēṇṭum.
eṭṭut tokiyuḷ kāṇappaṭum naṟṟiṇi, kuṟuntoki, aiṅkuṟunūṟu, patiṟṟuppattu, paripāṭal, kalittoki, akanāṉūṟu, puṟanāṉūṟu eṉṟa eṭṭaṉuḷ, puṟapporuḷ vakiyil amintavi patiṟṟuppattum, puṟanāṉūṟum eṉṟa iraṇṭumākum. iviyiraṇṭum, ēṉiyavaṟṟuḷ naṟṟiṇi, kalittoki yeṉṟa iraṇṭu moḻinta piṟa yāvum kālañ ceṉṟa perumpulavar ṭākṭar tiru. u. vē. cāminātiyaravarkaḷāl pala āṇṭukaṭku muṉpē pala ēṭukaḷiṉ tuṇi koṇṭu ārāyntu cevviya muṟiyil veḷiyiṭappeṟṟuḷḷaṉa. avaṟṟuḷ patiṟṟuppattu 1904-ām āṇṭil mutaṉmutalāka acciṭappeṟṟu veḷiyāyiṟṟu. ivvāṟē tamiḻakattut tamiḻaratu ilakkiyap paḻañcelvamāy, pala nūṟṟāṇṭukaṭku muṉ vāḻnta tamiḻ naṉmakkaḷuṭiya nākarikap paṇpāṭukaḷi yuṇarttum nalviḷakkamāyt tikaḻum intat toki nūlkaḷic cemmiyuṟa ārāyntu iṉṟum eṉṟum tamiḻ payilvōr aṉivarum orumukamākap pārāṭṭip paravattakka vakiyil veḷiyiṭuvatākiya ariya tamiḻppaṇi purinta ṭākṭar tiru. aiyaravarkaṭkut tamiḻulaku peritum kaṭamippaṭṭuḷatu.
tiru. aiyaravarkaḷ mutaṉmutalāka veḷiyiṭṭapōtē itaṟkup paṇṭic cāṉṟōr oruvar eḻutiya uriyum avarkku uṭaṉ kiṭittamiyiṉ, mutal veḷiyīṭṭilē patiṟṟuppattu mūlamum paḻiya vuriyum eṉa veḷiyiṭṭu, itaṉi aṟiñar kaṇṭu poruḷaṟintu iṉpuṟum vāyiliyum utaviyatu peritum pōṟṟattakkatākum. “ivvuri illi yāyiṉ, innūṟ poruḷi ikkālattil aṟintukoḷḷutal mika aritu” eṉa avarkaḷē urittiruppatu kāṇka. ēṭukaḷil urikārar peyar kuṟikkappaṭāmiyiṉ avar iṉṉāreṉṟu aṟivatu iyalātāyiṟṟu. āyiṉum, avar nēminātam ceyta kuṇavīra paṇṭitar kālattukkup piṟpaṭṭavareṉpatu orutali. patiṟṟuppattiṉ uriyil,cillērāḷareṉṟaviṭattuc “ciṉmiyic ciṉṉūl eṉṟatupōla īṇṭuc ciṟumiyākak koḷka” (patiṟ.76:1) eṉṟaviṭattu, urikārarāl ciṉṉūl eṉappaṭuvatu kuṇavīra paṇṭitar eḻutiya nēmināta meṉṉum nūlukkup peyar.
ivvaṇṇam pāṭṭum uriyumākak kiṭikkum ippatiṟṟup
pattu, mutaṟ pattum pattām pattum iṉṟi iṭiniṉṟa eṭṭup pattukkaḷē koṇṭuḷatu. kiṭikkum ēṭukaḷ palavaṟṟiṉum mutaṟ pattum iṟutip pattum kāṇappaṭavilli. pāṭṭum uriyum koṇṭa ēṭoṉṟil, oṉpatām pattiṉ iṟutiyil, “patiṟṟuppattu mūlamum uriyum muṭintatu; cupamastu” eṉṟu kāṇappaṭukiṟatu. mūlamēyuḷḷa ēṭukaḷum oṉpatām pattōṭē muṭikiṉṟaṉa. ivvāṟē toṭakkamum iraṇṭām pattiyē koṇṭu pala ēṭukaḷum uḷḷaṉa. itaṉāl neṭunāḷkaḷukku muṉpē, itaṉ mutaṟ pattum pattām pattum maṟintaṉa eṉak koḷḷa vēṇṭiyirukkiṟatu.
iṉi, kiṭittuḷḷa ovvoru pattukkum patikam oṉṟu kāṇappaṭukiṟatu. atu, pāṭappaṭṭa cēravēntaṉuṭiya meykkīrttipōl niṉṟu, pāṭiṉōr, pāṭappaṭṭōr, pāṭiya pāṭṭu, pāṭippeṟṟa paricil, pāṭappaṭṭa vēn taṉuṭiya āṭcik kālam eṉṟa ivaṟṟik kūṟukiṟatu. appatikaṅkaḷ, tām uṭkoṇṭu niṟkum pāṭṭukkaḷ ovvoṉṟukkum avvap pāṭṭiṉuṭ kāṇappaṭum coṟṟoṭa roṉṟāṟ peyar kuṟittuḷḷaṉa. ovvoru pāṭṭiṉ iṟutiyilum ap pāṭṭiṟkut  tuṟi, vaṇṇam, tūkku, peyar eṉṟa ivi vakukkappeṟṟuḷḷaṉa. ip peyarkaḷē patikattilum tokuttuk kāṭṭappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. mēlum, ip patikaṅkaḷ uriyuḷḷa ēṭukaḷiṟṟāṉ kāṇappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. paḻiyavuri ip patikaṅ kaṭkum uri kuṟittuḷḷatu. āṉāl, ip patikaṅkaḷ uriyillāta mūlappakutiyēyuḷḷa ēṭukaḷil illi. mūlamēyuḷḷa ēṭukaḷil ovvoru pāṭṭiṉ iṟutiyilum tuṟi, vaṇṇam, tūkku, peyar ākiyaṉa kuṟikkappeṟṟum, ov voru pattiṉ iṟutiyilum pāṭiṉōr peyarum pāṭap paṭṭōr peyarum, “imaya varampaṉ neṭuñ
cēralātaṉik kumaṭṭūrk kaṇṇaṉār pāṭiṉār pattuppāṭṭu muṟṟum” eṉṟāṟpōlak kuṟikkap peṟṟum uḷḷaṉa. ik kuṟippukkaḷi nōkkumiṭattu, patiṟṟuppattup pāṭṭukkaḷit tokut tōrāl vaṇṇam, tūkku, tuṟi, peyar ākiyaṉa vakukkap peṟṟirukkalāmeṉṟum, avarkkup piṉ vanta cāṉṟōr oruvarāl patikaṅkaḷ pāṭic cērkkap peṟṟirukkalā meṉṟum, karututaṟku iṭamuṇṭākiṟatu. ṭākṭar tiru. aiyaravarkaḷum, “ovvoru ceyyuḷiṉ piṉṉum amintuḷḷa tuṟi, vaṇṇam, tūkku, peyareṉpavikaḷ uriyillāta mūlap piratikaḷilellām iruttaliṉ, avi uriyāciriyarāl eḻutappaṭṭaṉa valla
veṉṟum, nūlāciriyarkaḷālō tokut tōrālō eḻutappaṭṭaṉaveṉṟum; patikaṅkaḷ urip piratikaḷil maṭṭum kāṇappaṭukiṉṟamiyāl avaṟṟi iyaṟṟiṉōr  nūlāciriyarallareṉṟum terikiṉṟaṉa. āciriyar nacciṉārkkiṉi yarālum aṭiyārkku nallārālum; tattam urikaḷil eṭuttāḷap peṟṟiruttaliṉ; ippatikaṅkaḷ avarkaḷ kālattiṟku muntiyaviyeṉṟu tōṟṟu kiṉṟatu” eṉṟu kūṟuvatu nōkkattakkatu.
cumār patiṉintu āṇṭukaṭkumuṉ ceṉṉip palkalik kaḻaka vittuvāṉ tērvukkuc celvōr cilarukku ip patiṟṟuppattiṉik kaṟpikkavēṇṭiya kaṭami eṉakku uṇṭāyiṟṟu. akkālattē avarkaṭku itaṉik kaṟpittu varukiyil, itaṟkoru virivuri yiruppiṉ nalamākumeṉum eṇṇamuṇṭāka; eṉ naṇpar cilar vāyilākap patiṟṟup pattiṉ ēṭukaḷ iraṇṭu peṟṟu, accuppaṭiyiyum avaṟṟiyum oppu nōkkuvatu mutaṟkaṇ ceyaṟpālateṉa uṇarntu ceytatil cila pāṭavēṟupāṭukaḷum, cila pāṭaṅkaḷiṟ kāṇappaṭṭa aiyaṅkaṭkut teḷivum kiṭittaṉa. piṉṉar ivvurip paṇiyi mēṟkoṇṭu ceytuvaruṅkāl, tiruvi yāṟṟu aracar kallūrip pērāciriyarum eṉ vaṇakkat tiṟkuriya āciriyarumākiya karantik kaviyaracu. tiru.  R. vēṅkaṭācalam piḷḷiyavarkaḷ tām eḻutivittirunta uri yiṉiyum tantu utaviṉārkaḷ. yāṉ eḻuti vittirunta uriyi nāvalar tiru. na. mu. vēṅkaṭacāmi nāṭṭāravarkaḷ pārviyiṭṭu ippōtu veḷiyāki yirukkum inta muṟiyik kāṭṭi ivvakiyil ivvuriyi yamikkumāṟu terivittārkaḷ.
ivvuriyiṉ amitiyi nēriṟ kaṇṭu ūkkiyatōṭu viriya acciṭuvatu nalameṉṟu teruṭṭiya eṅkaḷ arumpeṟal āciriyar tiru. na. mu. vēṅkaṭacāmi nāṭṭāravarkaḷ, itaṉ patikaṅkaḷ ārāyccikku iṭamāka vuḷḷaṉavātalāl, avaṟṟukku uri vēṇṭāveṉap paṇittamiyiṉ, innūṟ kaṇ patikaṅkaṭku uri yeḻutappaṭavilli. mēlum itaṉ mutaṟ pattu kiṭik kāmiyiṉ, itaṟku muṉṉaṇiyil kaṭavuḷ vāḻttuc ceyyuḷ oṉṟu iruntirukku meṉṟum, “eriyeḷḷuvaṉṉa niṟattaṉ” eṉat toṭaṅkuvatum, tol kāppiyap poruḷatikāravuriyil urikārarāṟ kāṭṭap paṭuvatumākiya pāṭṭi ip patiṟṟup pattiṉ kaṭavuḷ vāḻttuc ceyyuḷākak kōttu uri yeḻutumāṟum avarkaḷ urittārkaḷ. uri muḻutum accāki veḷivarum in nāḷil avarkaḷ illāmi eṉ maṉatti varuttukiṟatu.
iṉi, innūliṉ patikaṅkaḷukku uri yeḻutap paṭāmiyāl, ivaṟṟiṉ karuttu viḷaṅka oru kōvippaṭutti varalāṟṟu muṟiyil oru kaṭṭuri yeḻutic cērppatu nalameṉa ivvuriyik kaṇṭa aṟiñar kūṟiṉar. iv varalāṟṟut tuṟiyil yāṉ aṟinta nāṇmutal uḻittup perumpayaṉ tamiḻulakiṟkaḷittu varupavar eṉ arumpeṟal naṇpar  tiru. T.V. catācivap paṇṭārattāravarkaḷātalāl, avarkaḷi itaṉic ceyyumāṟu vēṇṭik koṇṭēṉ. avarkaḷum tamakkuḷḷa aluvalkaṭkiṭiyē uṭal valiyiṉmiyum poruṭ paṭuttātu patikap pakutipaṟṟiya ciṟanta ārāycci yuriyiṉi vaḻaṅki yuḷḷaṉar. avarkaṭku eṉ maṉaṅkeḻumiya naṉṟi yuriyatākiṉṟatu.
iṉi, yāṉ eḻutiya uriyi yāṉē ārāyntu nalan tīṅku kāṇpateṉpatu ciṟitu arumiyāka iruntamiyiṉ, uri kaṇṭa eṉṉip pōlavē pala āṇṭukaḷ vittuvāṉ tērvukkuc celvōrkku itaṉik kaṟpikkum paṇi mēṟkoṇṭu kūrtta pulamiyāl ciṟantu niṟkum eṉ ariya naṇpar tiru. ka. veḷḷi vāraṇaravarkaḷi uripaṟṟiyatoru kaṭṭuri tarumāṟu kēṭṭuk koṇṭēṉ. ataṉi maṟātu ēṟṟu aḻakiya kaṭṭuri tanta avarkaṭkum eṉ maṉamārnta naṉṟi yuriya tākiṉṟatu.
pallavar, cōḻar, pāṇṭiyar eṉṟa iv vēntarkaḷippaṟṟiya varalāṟukaḷēṉum ōraḷavil makkaḷ aṟintu kōṭaṟ kēṟṟa vakiyil nūlvaṭivil veḷiyāki irukkiṉṟaṉa. paṇṭi nāḷic cēra maṉṉarkaḷippaṟṟiya varalāṟṟiṉic cevvē aṟintukōṭaṟku vēṇṭum karuvikaḷākac caṅkat toki nūl kaṭku vēṟāka yātum kiṭittilatu. iṭikkālak kalveṭṭukkaḷ paṇṭic caṅka kālattuc cērar varalāṟṟukkut tuṇi ceyvaṉa vāka illi. cēranāṭṭu moḻiyum naṭiyum oḻukalāṟum palvēṟu makkaḷ kūṭṭuṟavāl vēṟupaṭ ṭoḻintami itaṟkuk kāraṇamām; āyiṉum, iṉṟiya kēraḷa nāṭṭiṉ paṇṭiya varalāṟṟiṉi ārāyntaṟitaṟku vēṇṭum karuvikaḷum kiṭittila; kiṭikkac ceytārumilli. ataṉāl ivvurikkaṇ teḷivikkappaṭum varalāṟṟuk kuṟippukkaḷ muṭinta muṭipākak kōṭaṟku iṭamilli yeṉpatu teḷivām. vēṟu ārāyccikaḷāl viḷakkamākuṅkāṟum, ivaṟṟi mēṟ kōṭal takkatu. immuyaṟcikkut tuṇiceyta naṇparum, 1941il vaṭavārkkāṭṭil cillāk kalvit talivarāka iruntavarumāṉa tiru. irāmaṉ mēṉaṉ avarkaṭku eṉ naṉṟiyuriyatākum.
ivvuri yeḻuti muṭikkappeṟṟatu cila pala āṇṭukaṭku muṉpēyeṉiṉum, iraṇṭāvatu ulakappōr kāraṇamāka, accēṟṟi veḷiyiṭuvateṉpatu ariya ceyalāyiṟṟu. an nerukkaṭi ippōtum tīrntu paṇṭupōl oḻintilatāyiṉum, ittakiya cīriya centamiḻnūl veḷiyīṭukaḷil caliyātu uḻittut, tamiḻakattiṟkum, tamiḻmoḻikkum peruntoṇṭu purintu ciṟakkum teṉṉintiya civa cittānta nūṟpatippuk kaḻakam, ivvuriyiṉi veḷiyiṭac camintatu kuṟittup potuvāka ataṟkum, ciṟappāka ataṉip palavaki uyar paṇikaḷil īṭupaṭutti avvāṟṟāl aḵtu ulavāp perumpukaḻ uṇmit tamiḻniliyamākat tikaḻacceytu mēmpaṭum kaḻakac ceyalmuṟit talivar tiru. va. cuppiyā piḷḷiyavar kaṭkum tamiḻakattiṉ cārpil eṉ uḷam niṟinteḻum naṉṟi yiṉit terivittuk koḷḷukiṉṟēṉ.
iṅkē kuṟitta tiruvāḷarkaḷēyaṉṟi vēṟuvakiyil tuṇiceyta palarkkum eṉ naṉṟiyic celuttum kaṭami yuṭiyēṉ. palvakiyilum kuṟipāṭuṭi yaṉākiya eṉṉi, eṉ arumit tamiḻaṉṉikkut toṇṭaṉākki āṭ koṇṭaruḷum enti, tilli maṉṟilniṉṟu tiruvaruṭ kūttiyaṟṟum āṭalaracaṉ tiruvaṭip pōtukaḷi maṉa moḻi meykaḷāṟ paravi yamikiṉṟēṉ.
aṇṇāmalinakar,
